par-p01-v01.speaker: Kṣemarāja (venerating voice)
par-p01-v01.question: What consciousness is venerated, and under which form?
premises: Veneration to Śiva, whose self is all tattvas without remainder (oṃ namaḥ śivāya nikhilatattvātmane).
The work avowed: the Entering-into-the-Supreme, Kṣemarāja-composed (atha parāprāveśikā ...viracitā).
The vow: consciousness venerated as the Lord's heart — world-formed yet transcending, throbbing as supreme power.
par-p01-v01.inference: Immanence and transcendence predicated together before any exposition; the paradox is the program.
uncertainties: Authorship: KSTS/Muktabodha ascribe to Kṣemarāja; Hareesh ascribes to Nāgānanda — edition followed, dispute logged (internal maṅgala + colophon support the edition).
Parādi read as supreme-etc. (threefold Śakti scale), not expanded.

par-p02-v02.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin; objector staged via nanu)
par-p02-v02.question: Bare shining, or shining that knows its shining?
premises: Thesis: the Lord is light-selfed; light is awareness-natured (prakāśātmā, vimarśasvabhāvaḥ).
Objection: granted light-nature, why not mere-knowing-nature like the calm-brahman teachers (nanu... śāntabrahmavādināmiva)?
Reply: awareness twofold (bounded/unbounded) and three-functioned (emission/maintenance/withdrawal as full-I-joy); maxim: flashing as the unmade I.
Consequence: awareness-less shining falls lordless and inert — sun proved (yadi nirvimarśaḥ... sūryādi).
par-p02-v02.inference: Calm-brahman bare light refused; awareness-less shining falls inert, sun-proved.
uncertainties: parimita/aparimita introduced to block the void-knower ceiling, left undeveloped.
Sun analogy extends by parity of reason, not identity.

par-p03-v03.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin)
par-p03-v03.question: One author's coinage, or the canon's constant theme?
premises: The list: this very awareness trumpeted in the āgamas by ten names (cit ... spandaḥ, ityādi).
The canon claim: awareness-primacy in consciousness-light trumpeted in each āgama, recited in differing āgama-speeches.

The justifications: each name defined by its office — chief-form, speech, ground-fullness, join-loose-lower, no-other-needed, yogin-like raising, mine-flashing, untrifling, rest-ground, still-shimmer.
par-p03-v03.inference: One awareness-primacy across scriptures; ten names each denote by office.
uncertainties: List open (ityādi) — no completeness claimed.
sarvasarvajñatā reductio secures sphurattā's mineness — kept as stated.

par-p04-v04.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin; two objections staged via nanu)
par-p04-v04.question: Granted awareness, does the Lord shine as the world — His doing, non-inert, unveilable?
premises: Shining: the unmade-I Lord throbs and shines by the Lady's power in śiva-to-earth world-form.
Doership + aliveness: this itself His world-making and its non-inertness.
Objection 1 (effecthood, bheda/abheda) → reply: effecthood just is shining-dependence (etadadhīnaprakāśatva); difference displayed, never real.
Usage argument: were the known different, unshining would unmake shining — nothing would be.
Objection 2 (veiling by likeness) → reply: the veil destroys itself; never veiled; life-breath cannot throttle.
par-p04-v04.inference: Effecthood means shining-dependence; likeness cannot veil — the world His life-breath.
uncertainties: Kāryatva replaced by shining-talk — noted, not imported beyond text.
Veil self-destruction asserted as self-evident (pratyuta).
etad = the aforementioned doership/Vimarśa (Pradipaka comparison); tirodhīyate print (Pradipaka's nirodh- variant noted).

par-p05-v05.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin)
par-p05-v05.question: If the Lord is self-shining, what work is left for proof?
premises: Already-proved: indicators and causes cannot operate on the before-proved Lord; even the injunction-making knower's standing needs no proof (tādrūpyeṇa sattvāt).
Two self-answering questions: thing's being assented; such-nature proved by the asker's own form (svasaṃvedana).
Proof's remaining office: ordained for māyā-dealings only; all else, inert, cannot light itself — how settle another?
Seal (taduktam): proofs stretch as things' life; beyond them the further Life, the Lord.
par-p05-v05.inference: Proof retired without retiring reasoning: self-proved, self-answered, demoted to māyā-traffic, outlived by Life.
uncertainties: svasaṃvedana taken as proving (text's move); asker-as-evidence.
pramāṇavarāka polemic color kept, not sharpened.

par-p06-v06.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin)
par-p06-v06.question: How is supreme Śiva — pure I-grasping — at once the thirty-sixfold expanse?
premises: Ground: His essence full-I-grasping made of word-mass — Śiva Himself the 36-formed expanse.
Word-mass: letter-heap a-to-ha enwombing all world; full I-grasp 'I alone light-selfed in shining,' freedom faceless.
Definition: tattva = the one undivided shining causing divided classes' classing (hill-earth, river-water).
List: the thirty-six names in order, bare.
par-p06-v06.inference: Phonemic fullness grounds plurality; undivided shine families the divided; roll bare.
uncertainties: List bare here; marks follow in p07–p08 (promissory structure).
śabdarāśi assumes mātṛkā doctrine without exposition.

par-p07-v07.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin)
par-p07-v07.question: How do the pure levels dim into personhood, bind and unbind, and wear five sheaths?
premises: Śiva-tattva: will-knowledge-action-formed pure-full-bliss, throbbing full-I-joy in all knowers, bearing lakh-fold reflections.
First throb (will-to-emit taken): will-power-tattva — freedom's greatness, outward-bloom-wish, bliss-surplus, 'I' grasped.

Dimming ladder: just-sprouting world I-covered (sadāśiva, will-chief, faint this) → sprouted world I-wrapped (īśvara, knowing-chief, clarified this) → I-this oneness (śuddhavidyā, doing-chief); single variable: this-portion faintness.
Māyā: difference-spreading among own-natured things, hardest feat, knower-pride in void, material cause of art-to-earth.
Person/bondsman: Lord veiling own-form by māyā-power (freedom's synonym), contracted-knowerness; deemed chains; wandering (body through ages, intellect across births).
Magician immunity: nondifferent, yet His delusion never the Lord's — self-willed illusion.
Freed (ciddhana): recognition-brought sovereignty, body-world as pure feeling, freed-bodied, Śiva at fall.
Five glories → five littles on robbed-king terms (respective pairing).
par-p07-v07.inference: Fall and return in one movement: dimming, masking, immunity, recognition, dealt-back powers.
uncertainties: dhyāmala/adhyāmala grading literal; śāstra-internal check welcome.
Two-phase release (freed-bodied vs Śiva-at-fall) both kept.
Glory→sheath respective pairing (kalā←doership etc.) standard doctrine.

par-p08-v08.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin)
par-p08-v08.question: What does each sheath take away, and how does nature unfold into organ, sense, subtle, gross?
premises: Five deprivations: little-doership (kalā), little-knowing (vidyā), clinging (rāga, may-I-grow-never-cease), sequence-cutting (kāla, was-am-will), must (niyati, mine-to-do).
One sheath: fivefold, veiling own-form, distinct-yet-undistinct over full consciousness.
Prakṛti: guṇa equipoise past telling apart; root-cause of great-to-earth.
Inner organ: deciding intellect, prideing ego, resolving mind — guṇa-effect, sense-gross-cause.
Ten senses in order; five commons (that-nothing-more); five element-offices.
par-p08-v08.inference: Deprivation then unfolding: littles, one cover, poise, organ, senses, commons, elements.
uncertainties: Five-as-one-sheath kept as stated.
tanmātra negative definition (tadeva nādhikam); no positive content added.

par-p09-v09.speaker: Kṣemarāja (siddhāntin; tradition-verse voiced)
par-p09-v09.question: Where do the thirty-six stand — inside what seed, by what proofs?
premises: Two similes: banyan-seed fitting bodies; peacock-egg-juice craft for the attentive.
Tradition-verse (āmnāya): power-formed great tree in banyan seed; moving-unmoving world in heart-seed shaped as supreme Lady.
Two proofs: pot-bowl→clay; liquid-kinds→water-common; so earth-to-māyā→being itself.
Involution: sat stripped to bare sa (primary-nature, not tattva 13) holding thirty-one; pure levels into assent-au; visarga emission above-below.
Double-formed seed (mantra-great, world-shaped, world-past) is Śiva as His own seat.
Fruit: knowing-entering initiates truly (oblation-void); living-freed; Śiva at fall; colophon.
par-p09-v09.inference: All inside the heart-seed, letter by letter proved; knowing-entering initiates without rite.
uncertainties: 31-in-sa / levels-in-au partition assumed as printed, untabulated.
visarga closes the emission arc (p02) — noted as closure.

par-p01-v01.plain_english: Veneration to Śiva, whose very self is all the levels of reality. Here begins the Entering-into-the-Supreme, composed by glorious Kṣemarāja, noblest of the great Māheśvara teachers. We bow to consciousness itself — the heart of the supreme Lord — which has the world for its form and yet goes beyond it, pulsing in the shape of supreme power.
par-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: viśvātmikāṃ taduttirṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ parameśituḥ parādiśaktirūpeṇa sphurantīṃ saṃvidaṃ numaḥ

par-p02-v02.plain_english: The supreme Lord, here, is made of light — and light is made of awareness. An objector asks: granted He is light by nature, why should He not be bare knowing, the way the calm-brahman teachers have it? The answer specifies awareness two ways — bounded and boundless — so that the bounded knower of the void does not put a ceiling on consciousness-light. In creating, awareness wears the world's shape; in sustaining, it shines the world forth; in withdrawing, it takes all back into itself — everywhere the thrill of a full and complete I. Awareness, in short, is the flash of an I that was never put together — through world-shaping, world-lighting, world-dissolving. And if that awareness were missing, lordlessness and deadness would follow — as sunlight, which lacks awareness, leans on something else to shine and sinks to the side of the inert.
par-p02-v02.sanskrit_cite: iha khalu parameśvaraḥ prakāśātmā, prakāśaśca | vimarśasvabhāvaḥ, vimarśo | akṛtrimāham iti visphuraṇam | nirvimarśaḥ syāt anīśvaro jaḍaśca

par-p03-v03.plain_english: This very awareness is what the scriptures trumpet under many names: consciousness, consciousness-in-its-freedom, the supreme Word risen from its own sap, freedom, the supreme Self's sovereign majesty, doership, pulsing, essence, heart, vibration — and more. In the Śaiva teaching, the scriptures everywhere proclaim one thing: that awareness comes first in the light of consciousness, sung in scripture after scripture in different words. Consciousness — because awareness is the Self's own chief form. The supreme Word — because it speaks the world into declaration by grasping it back, supreme as the ground and fullness of all lesser graspings, risen from its own sap because its "I" never sets, full-bodied consciousness. Freedom — because it binds the cast-out "this" back to the self, looses it again, and lays it low through the stations of the void — differing from the inert by exactly these marks. Sovereignty — needing nothing else when the world begins, unlike Brahmā and his fellow wardens of māyā's womb, who answer to another's will and bend to fate. Doership — raising the whole world, from Śiva down to earth, into "this"-ness out of inward shining oneness, the way a yogin makes things — an unsurpassed kind of causing. Pulsing — the relation of flashing, and it is mine: were throbbing nobody's in particular, everything would flash for everyone always, and all would be omniscient, or all blind. Essence — the untrifling form, the Lord's own power of awareness. Heart — where the world comes to rest. Vibration — the still light of consciousness shimmering with motion, the world appearing as something extra where nothing extra is.
par-p03-v03.sanskrit_cite: eṣa eva ca vimarśaḥ | vimarśaprādhānyameva tattadāgameṣu samuddhuṣṭaṃ, | ato mama sphuratīti madīyaṃ sphuraṇamāviṣṭa ityarthaḥ | acalasya citprakāśasya calattābhāsanaṃ,

par-p04-v04.plain_english: And therefore — the unmade I, real, self-lit in form — the supreme Lord pulses and shines by the power of the supreme Lady, taking the shape of the world from Śiva down to clay. This very shining is His making of the world — and the world's being alive. But what kind of "made" is the world — made as something different from Him, or as nothing different? If different, His freedom breaks; if not different, how is it made at all? The answer: without another's light the world cannot even be noticed, let alone come into its own — its coming to wear a shining body, leaning on His ground, is exactly what "made" means here. Māyā's own freedom puts difference on display, so the world is handled as different while being nothing different. "Made," in the end, means nothing but shining-by-Him. Formed this way, the world is nothing apart from Maheśvara the maker, who is shining-formed. For if what is known stood apart, it could not shine, and no shining could reach it — there would be nothing at all, and all the traffic of taking and giving would collapse. And if the world is nothing apart from the Lord, must He not be stained by resemblance to a merely shining world — veiled by it? Rather the would-be veil destroys itself: gained even within the self, veiling the light would unmake itself. By this world, then, the Lord's light-formed nature is never veiled — the world, given rest by His shining, has become His very life-breath. How could it throttle Him — and throttling Him, itself go on standing?
par-p04-v04.sanskrit_cite: akṛtrimāhamiti satattvaḥ svayaṃprakāśarūpaḥ parameśvaraḥ pārameśvaryā śaktyā śivādi dharaṇyantajagadātmanā sphurati prakāśate ca | kāryatvamapi etadadhīnaprakāśatvameva, | na kadācit tirodhīyate,

par-p05-v05.plain_english: Indicators and causes cannot get a grip on the Lord, proved before all proof — and since even the knower who lays down injunctions exists in His likeness, that knower's standing proved does not hang on any proof. His self-lit-ness is proved by experience. "What proves that He is?" — grant that things are. "What proves one of such a nature?" — the proof is the questioner's own shape: the self-shining of Maheśvara, proved before all, is proved for everyone by feeling oneself. Consciousness-light itself, the life of everything, appoints proofs for the business of illusion — but for Him no proof is ever used, since everything else, being inert, cannot light even itself without another's light, let alone settle anything beyond itself. Proof itself is proof only by leaning on Him — and for the proving of Him, who is proof's own life, what use is poor proof, whose office is to let some fresh flash come to rest, marked as a finding, inside the knower? The knower, ever-lit, his shining unbroken, already enjoys every finding tucked inward within himself — where would a fresh flash be put to use in him, and where else could its finding come to rest? So proof is for knowables like body and breath, blue and pleasure — not for the Lord, who is proof's life. Hence the saying: the proofs that draw out the very life of things — beyond them all stands a further Life, and He is the supreme Lord.

par-p06-v06.plain_english: And so — His essence being the full grasp of I, woven of the mass of sounds — supreme Śiva Himself is the whole display in thirty-six levels. The mass of sounds is the heap of letters from a to ha, pregnant with the entire world — the full I-grasp of the form "I alone, light-natured, in the shining," freedom resting with no other face to look to. And a level of reality is this: the one undivided shine that makes divided families into families — as hill and tree and town all show the form of earth, and river and lake and sea the form of water. The thirty-six: Śiva, power, eternal Śiva, the Lord, pure knowledge, illusion, art, knowing, passion, time, necessity, the person, nature, intellect, ego, mind, the five senses of knowing, the five senses of doing, the five subtles, the five gross elements.
par-p06-v06.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca śabdarāśimayapūrṇāhantāparāmarśasāratvāt | tasya bhāvastattvam iti bhinnānāṃ vargāṇāṃ vargīkaraṇanimittaṃ yadekamavibhaktaṃ bhāti tattattvam,

par-p07-v07.plain_english: Now what each is like. The Śiva-level is supreme Śiva Himself — will, knowing, and doing in one form, pure and full bliss by nature — throbbing within every knower as full-I joy, beyond every level, vast-bodied light that can hold a hundred thousand reflections of world-makings and world-unmakings. When the Lord takes on the will to send the world forth, His first pulse is already will-power's level — out of His own freedom's greatness, wishing to bloom outward, brimming with supreme-bliss joy, the grasp "I": power's level. The world, just now sprouting, stands covered over with I-by-the-self — the eternal-Śiva level: with the this-portion bloomed faintly upon the ground of pure consciousness only, will comes first. The sprouted world, standing wrapped in I — the Lord level: the I sprinkled over a clarified this, knowing comes first, the two differing only in how dim or undim the this-portion is. The grasp of I-and-this as one is pure knowledge: when, amid full-grown difference flashing, the I shines up as nothing but consciousness, the scales-held-even "I-this" grasp — doing comes first: knowledge's level. Spreading difference among things already of His own nature is illusion: achieving the hardest of feats, growing the pride of knowerhood in the unconscious and the void, making even one-with-consciousness things appear divided, hiding their own form — and the stuff all things from art to clay are made of. But when the Lord, by the Lady's power of illusion — which is only another name for freedom — veils His own form and puts on the tight mask of knowerhood, He is called the person — Himself, deluded by illusion, bound by deeds, taking his deeds for his chains — the wanderer, wandering. Though nothing apart from the supreme Lord, His delusion is never the Lord's own — as the magician's self-willed trick fools the crowd but not the magician. But when knowledge shows Him His own form, and His sovereignty is brought to recognition — when He takes even body and world for nothing but dense feeling, unmixed with the unconscious — then, thick with consciousness, He is free: fit to be called free while still in the body, with no more bond of rebirth — and when the body falls, supreme Śiva nature itself — supreme Śiva Himself. His are all-making, all-knowing, fullness, deathlessness, all-pervading — and His powers, though never narrowed, take narrowing and appear as art, knowing, passion, time, necessity. It is as when a king seizes a man's whole fortune and then, out of pity, deals him back a pittance to live on: just so wakefulness, shrunk to a mote and robbed of all-knowing, is dealt art and the rest instead — a little making to stand in for all-making.

par-p08-v08.plain_english: Art is what makes him do a little — a pot or two — who cannot do all. Knowing is what makes him know a little — the pot before him, not the thing far away. Passion is the clinging to things — "being incomplete and apart, may this serve me; may I grow; may I never cease" — in that shape. Time is what cuts the sequence of things as they shine and unshine — "I knew, I know, I will know; I did, I do, I will do" — measuring even things in the shape of knowing and doing, it cuts them off: past and the rest. Necessity is what holds him to "this is mine to do, that is not mine to do" — manifold shapes of must, fixed fruit from fixed cause among them. These five, by veiling His own form, are called the sheath — other than His form, yet not other, lying over the nature of full consciousness like a cover. The root-cause of the levels from the great down to earth is nature — goodness, passion, and darkness in equipoise: pleasure, pain, and delusion by make, shining, doing, and holding by nature — an undivided poise where part and counterpoint cannot be told apart. What decides — "this is such" — holding the mirror up to passing thoughts, fit by clarity to catch reflections, is intellect. What means "mine, not mine" in pride is ego. What means resolve is mind. These three are the inner organ — grasping inner things like pleasure, made of the strands in part-and-counterpoint, and the cause of the sense-and-gross heap to come. The means of grasping sounds, touches, forms, tastes, smells in order are ear, skin, eye, tongue, nose — the five knowing senses. The means of speaking, taking, moving, voiding, and blissful action in order are voice, hands, feet, evacuation, generation — the five doing senses. Sounds, touches, forms, tastes, smells in their common shape — that and nothing more, with no inner distinctions — are the five subtles. Ether gives room; air keeps alive; fire burns and cooks; water refreshes and flows; earth upholds.

par-p09-v09.plain_english: As sprout and leaf and fruit stand in the banyan seed in bodies exactly fitted to them, so this whole world in all its varied makings stands inside the seed of the heart — as in peacock-egg juice the craftsman's skill already holds every feather's line and plume-variety, for those rich in attention to weigh with subtle sight. "As the great tree stands in the banyan seed in power-form, so this world, moving and unmoving, stands in the heart-seed": by this traditional maxim, in the heart-seed shaped as the supreme Lady this world is contained. How so? As the ultimate truth of pot and bowl, clay's transformations, is clay itself — as watery kinds, examined, settle into water-in-common — so the levels from earth to illusion, examined for what is real in them, prove to be being itself. Even of the word "being" itself: strip the suffix that shows the root's sense, and the bare-stem letter s alone is left — and inside it stand thirty-one levels; beyond it, pure knowledge, the Lord, and eternal Śiva, knowledge-and-action in essence, enter as special powers into the syllable au, shaped as assent, formed of unsurpassed power. Hence the supreme emission, shaped as creation above and below: the breath-out to be breathed. Of the heart-seed so formed — shaped as the great mantra, shaped as the world, beyond the world — supreme Śiva Himself, as the seat where all rising comes to rest, is its own nature: all-shapedness, then shapelessness, each in turn the cause. Whoever truly knows such a heart-seed, and enters it — he is initiated in the highest sense: this very knowing, with no sesame-and-ghee oblation, is initiation in truth. Still breathing, living as men live, he is free while living; and when the body falls, he becomes the Lord, supreme Śiva Himself.

lines: Veneration to Śiva, whose very self is every level of reality.
Here begins the Entering into the Supreme, by glorious Kṣemarāja, noblest of the great Māheśvara masters.
And we bow to knowing itself — the heart of the supreme Lord: it wears the world as its body, yet stands beyond the world, pulsing as supreme power.
par-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: viśvātmikāṃ taduttirṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ parameśituḥ parādiśaktirūpeṇa sphurantīṃ saṃvidaṃ numaḥ

lines: The supreme Lord is light through and through — and light, rightly seen, is awareness through and through.
"But why not bare knowing," comes the objection, "the calm brahman praised by the school of stillness?"
Because awareness is twofold — bound and boundless — lest the bounded knower, even of the void, set a ceiling on the light.
In creating it takes the world's shape; in keeping, it lights the world; in withdrawing, it gathers all back into itself — everywhere the delight of a whole and perfect I.
Awareness is simply this: the flash of an I nobody made — through shaping, shining, dissolving.
Take it away, and lordship goes with it, and deadness: sunlight, which knows nothing, must borrow its shining from another and sinks to the side of the inert.
par-p02-v02.sanskrit_cite: iha khalu parameśvaraḥ prakāśātmā, prakāśaśca | vimarśasvabhāvaḥ, vimarśo | akṛtrimāham iti visphuraṇam | nirvimarśaḥ syāt anīśvaro jaḍaśca

lines: Scripture trumpets this one awareness under ten working names — knowing, knowing-in-freedom, the high Word risen from its own sap, freedom, the Self's high sovereignty, making, pulsing, essence, heart, throb.

Each name is earned by what it does: knowing, for awareness is the Self's chief shape; the Word, for it speaks the world by grasping it back to itself, supreme as the ground and fullness of every lesser grasp, sap-risen since its "I" never sets; freedom, for it binds the cast-out "this" home and looses it and lays it low through the hollow places, and by these marks is known from the inert; sovereignty, for it needs no other when the world begins — no fate-bound Brahmā warden answering to another's will; making, for it lifts the whole world from Śiva to clay into "this," the way a yogin makes, out of one inward shining; pulsing, for the flash is always someone's — were throbbing no one's in particular, all would blaze for all, and all be all-knowing or all blind; essence, the untrifling shape, the Lord's own power of knowing; heart, where the world comes to rest; throb, the still light stirring, the world showing as something extra where nothing extra is.
par-p03-v03.sanskrit_cite: eṣa eva ca vimarśaḥ | vimarśaprādhānyameva tattadāgameṣu samuddhuṣṭaṃ, | ato mama sphuratīti madīyaṃ sphuraṇamāviṣṭa ityarthaḥ | acalasya citprakāśasya calattābhāsanaṃ,

lines: So the unmade I — real, lit by itself — the Lord pulses and shines by his Lady's power in the shape of the world from Śiva to clay.
This shining is his making, and the world's being alive.
"But made how — as something other than him, or as nothing other?" As other, his freedom breaks; as nothing other, what is there to make?
The answer: without another's light the world cannot so much as be noticed, let alone come into its own — its coming to bear a shining body, leaning on his ground, is exactly what "made" means.
Difference is put on display by freedom's own magic, so the world is handled as different while being nothing different: to be made is to shine by him, and nothing else.
Formed this way the world is nothing apart from Maheśvara the maker.
For stood the known apart, it could not shine and no shining could reach it — there would be nothing at all, and all the give and take of the world would fall.
"Then must he not be stained by likeness, veiled by a shining world?" Rather the would-be veil unmakes itself: caught even inside the self, in veiling light it vanishes.
By this world his light-shape is never veiled — the world, given rest by his shining, has grown into his very breath.
How should it choke him — and choking him, itself go on standing?

lines: Signs and causes cannot lay a finger on the Lord, proved before all proving — and since even the knower who lays down the law stands in his likeness, that knower's standing needs no proof.
His self-lit-ness is proved by undergoing.
"What proves that he is?" — grant that things are.
"What proves one of such a nature?" — the proof is the asker's own shape: Maheśvara's self-shining, proved before all, is proved for each by feeling himself.

The light of knowing, life of everything, appoints proofs for the market of illusion — but for him no proof is ever spent: all else, being inert, cannot light even itself without another's light, let alone settle anything beyond.

Proof is proof only by leaning on him; and for proving him, who is proof's own life, what use is poor proof, whose whole office is to let some fresh flash come to rest, stamped as a finding, inside the knower?
The knower, ever lit, his shining unbroken, already enjoys every finding tucked inward in himself — where would a fresh flash find work in him, and where else could its finding rest?
So proof is for knowables — body, breath, blue, delight — not for the Lord, who is proof's life.
Hence the saying: the proofs that draw out the very life of things — beyond them all stands a further Life, and he is the supreme Lord.

lines: Now their marks, each in turn.

The Śiva-level is Śiva himself — will, knowing, and doing in a single shape, pure and whole delight by nature — pulsing inside every knower as whole-I joy, past every level, vast-bodied light that can hold a hundred thousand reflections of world-makings and unmakings.

When the Lord takes up the will to send the world out, his first pulse is already will-power's level — out of his freedom's greatness, longing to bloom outward, brimming with high-bliss joy, the grasp "I": power's level.
The world, just budding, stands covered in I-by-the-self — the ever-Śiva level, the "this"-share bloomed faint on pure knowing-ground, will foremost.
The budded world, standing wrapped in I — the Lord level, the I dusted over a cleared "this," knowing foremost, the two differing only in how faint or clear the "this"-share is.
The grasp of I-and-this as one is pure knowing: where amid full-grown difference the I shines up as nothing but knowing, the even-held "I-this" — doing foremost.

Difference spreading among things already of his own nature is illusion — the hardest feat of all: it fattens knower-pride in the unconscious and the void, shows even one-with-knowing things split apart, hides their own shape — and is the stuff everything from art to clay is made of.

But when the Lord, by the Lady's power of illusion, which is freedom under another name, veils his own shape and puts on the tight mask of the knower, he is called the person — himself, fooled by illusion, chained by deeds, calling his deeds his chains — the wanderer, wandering.
Though nothing apart from the Lord, his fooling is never the Lord's own — as the magician's trick, willed by himself, fools the crowd and never the magician.

But when knowing shows him his shape and his sovereignty is brought to recognition — when even body and world are taken as nothing but pure feeling — dense with knowing, he is free: fit to be called free while still bodied, past the bond of rebirth; and when the body falls, Śiva-nature itself — Śiva himself.

His all-making, all-knowing, wholeness, deathlessness, everywhere-ness — powers unshrunk, taking shrinkage as art, knowing, passion, time, necessity: as a king robbed of everything is dealt a little back out of pity to live on, so wakefulness, shrunk to a point, robbed of all-knowing, is dealt art and the rest in its place, for the sake of a little making.

lines: Art is what lets him who cannot make all make a little — a pot or two.
Knowing is what lets him know a little — the pot before him, not the thing far off.
Passion is the sticker to things — "unwhole, apart, let this serve me; let me grow; let me never not be."

Time is what cuts the train of things as they shine and unshine — "I knew, I know, I shall know; I did, I do, I shall do" — measuring things too in knowing-doing shape, it cuts them off: past and the rest.
Must is what holds him to "this is mine to do, that is not" — the many shapes of must, fixed fruit from fixed cause among them.
These five, by veiling his own shape, are called the sheath — other than his shape yet not other, lying over whole-knowing-nature like a cover.

The root-cause of the levels from the great down to clay is nature — good, passion, dark in equipoise: pleasure, pain, fooling by make-up; shining, doing, holding by nature — one poise where part and counterpoint cannot be told apart.
What settles "this is so" — holding the mirror to passing thoughts, clear, fit to catch reflections — is intellect.
What says "mine, not mine" in pride is ego.
What says "I'll do it" is mind.
These three are the inner instrument — grasping inward things like pleasure, made of the strands in part-and-counterpoint, mother of the sense-and-element heap to come.
Ears, skin, eyes, tongue, nose in order take sounds, touches, shapes, tastes, smells — the five knowing senses.
Voice, hands, feet, the voider, the begetter in order do speaking, holding, moving, voiding, delighting — the five doing senses.
Sounds, touches, shapes, tastes, smells in their common shape — that and nothing more, with no between-marks — are the five subtles.
Room-giving is ether; life-stirring, air; burning and cooking, fire; freshening and flowing, water; upholding, earth.

"As the great tree stands in the banyan seed in power-shape, so this world, moving and unmoving, stands in the heart-seed": by this old maxim, in the heart-seed shaped as the high Lady, this world is held.

How so? As the last truth of pot and bowl, clay's shapings, is clay itself — as watery kinds, looked into, settle into water-in-common — so the levels from clay to illusion, weighed for what is real in them, prove to be being itself.

Even of the word "being" itself: shed the tail that shows the root's sense, and the bare letter s is left — and inside it stand thirty-one levels; beyond, pure knowing, the Lord, ever-Śiva, knowing-and-doing in essence, enter as powers apart into the letter au, shaped as assent, made of unsurpassed power.
Hence the high sending-forth, shaped as making above and below: the breath-out to be breathed.

Of the heart-seed so formed — shaped as the great chant, shaped as the world, past the world — Śiva himself, where all rising comes to rest, is its own nature: all-shapes, then no-shape, each in turn the cause.
Whoever truly knows such a heart-seed and walks into it is begun indeed — this very knowing, with no sesame-and-ghee poured on fire, is the true beginning.
Still drawing breath, dwelling as men dwell, he walks free while living; and when the body falls, he is the Lord, Śiva himself.
par-p09-v09.sanskrit_cite: nyagrodhabījasthaḥ śaktirūpo mahādrumaḥ tathā hṛdayabījasthaṃ viśvametaccarācaram | prakṛtimātrarūpaḥ sakāra evāvaśiṣyate, | tilājyāhutivarjitametatparijñānameva tattvato dīkṣā

lines: Veneration to Śiva, whose very self is every level of reality.
Here begins the Entering into the Supreme, by glorious Kṣemarāja, noblest of the great Māheśvara masters.
And we bow to knowing itself — the heart of the supreme Lord: it wears the world as its body, yet stands beyond the world, pulsing as supreme power.
par-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: viśvātmikāṃ taduttirṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ parameśituḥ parādiśaktirūpeṇa sphurantīṃ saṃvidaṃ numaḥ

lines: The supreme Lord is light through and through — and light, rightly seen, is awareness through and through.
"But why not bare knowing," comes the objection, "the calm brahman praised by the school of stillness?"
Because awareness is twofold — bound and boundless — lest the bounded knower, even of the void, set a ceiling on the light.
In creating it takes the world's shape; in keeping, it lights the world; in withdrawing, it gathers all back into itself — everywhere the delight of a whole and perfect I.
Awareness is simply this: the flash of an I nobody made — through shaping, shining, dissolving.
Take it away, and lordship goes with it, and deadness: sunlight, which knows nothing, must borrow its shining from another and sinks to the side of the inert.
par-p02-v02.sanskrit_cite: iha khalu parameśvaraḥ prakāśātmā, prakāśaśca | vimarśasvabhāvaḥ, vimarśo | akṛtrimāham iti visphuraṇam | nirvimarśaḥ syāt anīśvaro jaḍaśca

lines: Scripture trumpets this one awareness under ten working names — knowing, knowing-in-freedom, the high Word risen from its own sap, freedom, the Self's high sovereignty, making, pulsing, essence, heart, throb.

Each name is earned by what it does: knowing, for awareness is the Self's chief shape; the Word, for it speaks the world by grasping it back to itself, supreme as the ground and fullness of every lesser grasp, sap-risen since its "I" never sets; freedom, for it binds the cast-out "this" home and looses it and lays it low through the hollow places, and by these marks is known from the inert; sovereignty, for it needs no other when the world begins — no fate-bound Brahmā warden answering to another's will; making, for it lifts the whole world from Śiva to clay into "this," the way a yogin makes, out of one inward shining; pulsing, for the flash is always someone's — were throbbing no one's in particular, all would blaze for all, and all be all-knowing or all blind; essence, the untrifling shape, the Lord's own power of knowing; heart, where the world comes to rest; throb, the still light stirring, the world showing as something extra where nothing extra is.
par-p03-v03.sanskrit_cite: eṣa eva ca vimarśaḥ | vimarśaprādhānyameva tattadāgameṣu samuddhuṣṭaṃ, | ato mama sphuratīti madīyaṃ sphuraṇamāviṣṭa ityarthaḥ | acalasya citprakāśasya calattābhāsanaṃ,

lines: So the unmade I — real, lit by itself — the Lord pulses and shines by his Lady's power in the shape of the world from Śiva to clay.
This shining is his making, and the world's being alive.
"But made how — as something other than him, or as nothing other?" As other, his freedom breaks; as nothing other, what is there to make?
The answer: without another's light the world cannot so much as be noticed, let alone come into its own — its coming to bear a shining body, leaning on his ground, is exactly what "made" means.
Difference is put on display by freedom's own magic, so the world is handled as different while being nothing different: to be made is to shine by him, and nothing else.
Formed this way the world is nothing apart from Maheśvara the maker.
For stood the known apart, it could not shine and no shining could reach it — there would be nothing at all, and all the give and take of the world would fall.
"Then must he not be stained by likeness, veiled by a shining world?" Rather the would-be veil unmakes itself: caught even inside the self, in veiling light it vanishes.
By this world his light-shape is never veiled — the world, given rest by his shining, has grown into his very breath.
How should it choke him — and choking him, itself go on standing?
par-p04-v04.sanskrit_cite: akṛtrimāhamiti satattvaḥ svayaṃprakāśarūpaḥ parameśvaraḥ pārameśvaryā śaktyā śivādi dharaṇyantajagadātmanā sphurati prakāśate ca | kāryatvamapi etadadhīnaprakāśatvameva, | na kadācit tirodhīyate,

lines: Signs and causes cannot lay a finger on the Lord, proved before all proving — and since even the knower who lays down the law stands in his likeness, that knower's standing needs no proof.
His self-lit-ness is proved by undergoing.
"What proves that he is?" — grant that things are.
"What proves one of such a nature?" — the proof is the asker's own shape: Maheśvara's self-shining, proved before all, is proved for each by feeling himself.

The light of knowing, life of everything, appoints proofs for the market of illusion — but for him no proof is ever spent: all else, being inert, cannot light even itself without another's light, let alone settle anything beyond.

Proof is proof only by leaning on him; and for proving him, who is proof's own life, what use is poor proof, whose whole office is to let some fresh flash come to rest, stamped as a finding, inside the knower?
The knower, ever lit, his shining unbroken, already enjoys every finding tucked inward in himself — where would a fresh flash find work in him, and where else could its finding rest?
So proof is for knowables — body, breath, blue, delight — not for the Lord, who is proof's life.
Hence the saying: the proofs that draw out the very life of things — beyond them all stands a further Life, and he is the supreme Lord.

lines: His essence, then, is the whole grasp of I, woven of the mass of sound — so Śiva himself is the full display in thirty-six levels.
The mass of sound is the heap of letters from a to ha, pregnant with the entire world: the whole I-grasp in the shape "I alone, light-natured, in the shining" — freedom with no other face to look to.

And a level of reality is this: the one undivided shine that makes divided families into families — as hill and tree and town all show the shape of earth, and river and lake and sea the shape of water.

The thirty-six: Śiva, power, ever-Śiva, the Lord, pure knowing, illusion, art, knowing, passion, time, necessity, the person, nature, intellect, ego, mind, the five senses of knowing, the five of doing, the five subtles, the five great elements.
par-p06-v06.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca śabdarāśimayapūrṇāhantāparāmarśasāratvāt | tasya bhāvastattvam iti bhinnānāṃ vargāṇāṃ vargīkaraṇanimittaṃ yadekamavibhaktaṃ bhāti tattattvam,

lines: Now their marks, each in turn.

The Śiva-level is Śiva himself — will, knowing, and doing in a single shape, pure and whole delight by nature — pulsing inside every knower as whole-I joy, past every level, vast-bodied light that can hold a hundred thousand reflections of world-makings and unmakings.

When the Lord takes up the will to send the world out, his first pulse is already will-power's level — out of his freedom's greatness, longing to bloom outward, brimming with high-bliss joy, the grasp "I": power's level.
The world, just budding, stands covered in I-by-the-self — the ever-Śiva level, the "this"-share bloomed faint on pure knowing-ground, will foremost.
The budded world, standing wrapped in I — the Lord level, the I dusted over a cleared "this," knowing foremost, the two differing only in how faint or clear the "this"-share is.
The grasp of I-and-this as one is pure knowing: where amid full-grown difference the I shines up as nothing but knowing, the even-held "I-this" — doing foremost.

Difference spreading among things already of his own nature is illusion — the hardest feat of all: it fattens knower-pride in the unconscious and the void, shows even one-with-knowing things split apart, hides their own shape — and is the stuff everything from art to clay is made of.

But when the Lord, by the Lady's power of illusion, which is freedom under another name, veils his own shape and puts on the tight mask of the knower, he is called the person — himself, fooled by illusion, chained by deeds, calling his deeds his chains — the wanderer, wandering.
Though nothing apart from the Lord, his fooling is never the Lord's own — as the magician's trick, willed by himself, fools the crowd and never the magician.

But when knowing shows him his shape and his sovereignty is brought to recognition — when even body and world are taken as nothing but pure feeling — dense with knowing, he is free: fit to be called free while still bodied, past the bond of rebirth; and when the body falls, Śiva-nature itself — Śiva himself.

His all-making, all-knowing, wholeness, deathlessness, everywhere-ness — powers unshrunk, taking shrinkage as art, knowing, passion, time, necessity: as a king robbed of everything is dealt a little back out of pity to live on, so wakefulness, shrunk to a point, robbed of all-knowing, is dealt art and the rest in its place, for the sake of a little making.
par-p07-v07.sanskrit_cite: prathamaspanda evecchāśaktitattvam | indrajālamiva aindrajālikasya svecchayā saṃpāditabhrānteḥ, | yathā rājñāpahṛtasarvasvasya anukampayā jīvanārthaṃ kiṃcit stokaṃ dhanaṃ dīyate

lines: Art is what lets him who cannot make all make a little — a pot or two.
Knowing is what lets him know a little — the pot before him, not the thing far off.
Passion is the sticker to things — "unwhole, apart, let this serve me; let me grow; let me never not be."

Time is what cuts the train of things as they shine and unshine — "I knew, I know, I shall know; I did, I do, I shall do" — measuring things too in knowing-doing shape, it cuts them off: past and the rest.
Must is what holds him to "this is mine to do, that is not" — the many shapes of must, fixed fruit from fixed cause among them.
These five, by veiling his own shape, are called the sheath — other than his shape yet not other, lying over whole-knowing-nature like a cover.

The root-cause of the levels from the great down to clay is nature — good, passion, dark in equipoise: pleasure, pain, fooling by make-up; shining, doing, holding by nature — one poise where part and counterpoint cannot be told apart.
What settles "this is so" — holding the mirror to passing thoughts, clear, fit to catch reflections — is intellect.
What says "mine, not mine" in pride is ego.
What says "I'll do it" is mind.
These three are the inner instrument — grasping inward things like pleasure, made of the strands in part-and-counterpoint, mother of the sense-and-element heap to come.
Ears, skin, eyes, tongue, nose in order take sounds, touches, shapes, tastes, smells — the five knowing senses.
Voice, hands, feet, the voider, the begetter in order do speaking, holding, moving, voiding, delighting — the five doing senses.
Sounds, touches, shapes, tastes, smells in their common shape — that and nothing more, with no between-marks — are the five subtles.
Room-giving is ether; life-stirring, air; burning and cooking, fire; freshening and flowing, water; upholding, earth.

Fall-and-return in one movement; magician-immunity + robbed-king-dealing similes kept (both load-bearing); two-phase release both kept per UNC; grading literal per UNC. Rejected: (a) cutting one release phase → killed by UNC. (b) resolving dhyāmala grading → killed literal. (c) modernizing similes → killed: load-bearing. Read aloud: NOW their-MARKS, EACH in-TURN … AS a-KING robbed OF-ev-ery-THING is-DEALT a-LITT-le-BACK.

reads_against.argmap: How do the pure levels dim into personhood, bind and unbind, and wear five sheaths? → Fall and return in one movement: dimming, masking, immunity, recognition, dealt-back powers.
c1_essence: Pure bliss-nature throbbing with hundred-thousand reflections wills emission; will-first, knowing-first, doing-first dim by this-portion faintness; illusion spreads difference, stuffs art-to-earth, and veils by freedom's synonym into personhood — deemed-bound, wandering. The mask never touches the wearer (magician). Recognition restores sovereignty: dense-conscious, free-bodied, Śiva at fall. Five glories, uncontracted, accept contraction into five littles on robbed-king terms.

reads_against.argmap: What does each sheath take away, and how does nature unfold into organ, sense, subtle, gross? → Deprivation then unfolding: littles, one cover, poise, organ, senses, commons, elements.
c1_essence: Doing-a-little, knowing-a-little, clinging in may-I-grow-never-cease shape, sequence-cutting was-am-will, must in mine-to-do shape — five functions, one veil over full consciousness, distinct-yet-undistinct. Nature poises the three strands past telling apart. Deciding, prideing, resolving organ; ten senses ordered; five commons defined by having-nothing-more; five element-offices: room, life, burn-cook, refresh-flow, uphold.
